children: Waller cooled rate-hike fears, technology stocks rallied and bond yields retreated. Friday’s jobs report now gets an inconvenient opportunity to reconsider everything.
Wall Street gets its confidence back

The Nasdaq Composite surged 1.4% Thursday to 26,584.06, while the S&P 500 gained 1.1% to 7,747.71. The Dow climbed 624 points, or 1.2%, to 53,686.11. US futures were more restrained Friday as traders waited for the employment report.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller sparked the rally by saying he could support keeping rates unchanged if incoming data confirms inflation is easing. Markets cut the probability of a September increase from roughly 63% to 50%.
Treasury yields retreated from multi-year highs, easing pressure on equity valuations. Lower yields particularly benefit growth stocks because more of their expected profits sit in the future.
Discount those earnings at a smaller rate and today’s share price becomes easier to defend — at least until 8:30 a.m New York.
Technology leads the rebound

Nvidia gained 1.8% after agreeing to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. The deal gives Nvidia access to more than 18 million developers (users) while extending its influence beyond chips and into the models, tools and services built on top of them.
Snowflake closed 16.6% higher after its
beat and upgraded outlook, lifting Salesforce, ServiceNow and Adobe alongside it.
Broadcom moved the other way, falling 2.7% after its immediate revenue guidance missed expectations despite forecasting enormous long-term AI-chip growth.
Tesla added more than 5% before launching limited Cybercab rides in Austin. The steering-wheel-free robotaxi immediately attracted attention from US safety regulators.
Evidently, releasing an autonomous vehicle without pedals creates both future revenue possibilities and several very present regulatory questions.
Jobs report holds the final vote
August nonfarm payrolls are expected to show 56,000 new jobs, following July’s surprise loss of 23,000. Unemployment is forecast to remain at 4.1%.
Strong hiring could revive Fed tightening bets; another weak reading may replace rate anxiety with concerns about economic growth.
Asian shares followed Wall Street higher and global bonds stabilized. The dollar index held near 99, while USD/JPY dropped toward ¥155.50 as traders priced
. Gold stayed near $4,470 after Thursday’s 2% rebound and Bitcoin hovered around $81,000.
Brent crude traded near $95.70 and headed for a weekly gain above 7% as US-Iran tensions threatened Middle Eastern supply.
That leaves equities balancing softer yields against expensive energy. The ideal payroll number must now support growth, restrain rates and perhaps negotiate a ceasefire before lunch.
Good day on Wall Street
Tech powers higher
Rate fears cool

title: IXIC: Nasdaq Jumps 1.4% Before August Payrolls Put All-Out Rally to the Test
